content:
- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 3–5 days.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model often overcorrects in next 3–7 days; reduce forecast by 2–5% for 3–7 days.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (price drops sharply after peak), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast peak by 5–10% and shift downward slope.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate in early days (1–7) when sentiment is volatile; adjust downward by 1–3% for days 1–7.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model often misaligns with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
- When true outcome deviates from model by >5% in first 3 days, model often fails to correct; apply bias correction for next 5 days based on sentiment momentum.
